analysis: Examined the provider-side change in AppAttestKeyHistoryBuilder.swift (line 50) and the docs/threat-model.yaml changes. The code change replaces `$0 <= now` with `$0.timeIntervalSince(now) <= 0` in the 24h key-generation history filter. This is semantically equivalent for Date values (an attempt not later than now). NaN and infinite Dates are not a realistic input, and the other conjunct `now.timeIntervalSince($0) < generationWindow` is unchanged, so future-dated attempts are still excluded and the window is unchanged. It affects only diagnostic history counts (generationsLast24h), not the budget enforcement or authorization verdict. It does not touch A-015/A-016 proof verification, T-053 binding, or T-057 recovery. The threat-model patch adds a header comment about avoiding weak-imported Date operators (SDK 27.2) that crashed pre-release macOS 27.2 in a loop (availability), and mentions a release-build check script, scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py. That script is not in the supplied evidence, so I can't confirm its existence or behavior. Nonetheless this is a documentation claim about a control outside the batch, not a regression. The comment states the change leaves thresholds and results unchanged, consistent with the code. The head-text units for T-041 through T-061 are unchanged context in the supplied evidence (the file_changes range shows only the header lines 41-48 changed), and I saw no weakening of the cache, attestation, fan-helper, add-on hold or sandbox installer mitigations. Remaining integration question: other callers in the PR that use >=/<= on Dates (budget, enrollment resume, stall restart) were not supplied in this batch, so their equivalence is unverified.
